stories.title: FICCI calls for comprehensive India‑Africa trade framework ahead of minister’s Egypt visit
stories.summary: The Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) urged India and African nations to develop a comprehensive trade arrangement that would provide a predictable framework, reduce barriers and attract investment. FICCI Secretary General Anant Swarup highlighted the need for broader cooperation. The call was made as Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal prepares for a visit to Egypt, which FICCI sees as an opportunity to strengthen ties.
stories.why: A clear India‑Africa trade framework could increase bilateral trade and investment, supporting economic growth in both regions.

stories.title: Chinese open‑weight AI models show evidence of training on U.S.-banned Nvidia Blackwell GPUs
stories.summary: A study by Will DePue of the nonprofit Unemployment Labs examined the weight matrices of open‑weight large language models released by DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group. The analysis identified patterns that match the configurations of Nvidia’s Blackwell GPUs, which are prohibited from export to China. The article also notes that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang left the company after an affair was disclosed, and that Nvidia may still ship its less powerful H200 chip to China via a circuitous route permitted under existing export rules.
stories.why: It suggests possible violations of U.S. export controls, raising security and competitive concerns for the United States.

stories.title: Concurrent Gainers: 8 stocks gain for 5 days in a row
stories.summary: Around 23 stocks from the BSE 200 index advanced in all five consecutive sessions from November 8 to 13. Of these, we shortlisted 8 stocks that consistently gained throughout the period, delivering cumulative returns ranging from 7% to 11%.

stories.title: US assures India lower tariffs than peers in trade deal
stories.summary: The United States told India that, under the proposed trade agreement, India will receive tariff rates lower than those applied to other U.S. trading partners. The first phase of the deal will focus on tariff reductions for goods only. Tariff terms for services are slated to be negotiated in a later phase.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.
